bug_description.normalized:
Stage 01's saved 388-byte witness begins with the ASCII config prefix `dolang=e
encoding=utf-16

`, so Aspell normalizes the attacker-controlled encoding to `ucs-2` and builds `DecodeDirect<unsigned short>` for `speller->to_internal_`. `DocumentChecker::process()` then decodes the remaining 362-byte document through that wide decoder. In the vulnerable `DecodeDirect`, each UTF-16 code unit is appended to `FilterCharVector` with the default width 1 instead of width 2, so `TokenizerBasic` and `DocumentChecker::next_misspelling()` later compute `tok.offset` and `tok.len` in UTF-16 code units rather than bytes. The fuzzer reuses those values as raw byte arguments to `aspell_speller_suggest()`, whose `Convert::convert()` re-enters `DecodeDirect<unsigned short>::decode()`. On the crashing iteration that second decode receives an odd positive `size`; line 553 forms `stop` from `reinterpret_cast<const unsigned short *>(in0 + size)` and the 2-byte `++in` loop at line 555 never reaches that boundary, eventually reading 2 bytes at the first address past the 388-byte heap buffer. Commit `de29341638833ba7717bd6b5e6850998454b044b` fixes both obligations by recording `sizeof(Chr)` widths for wide decodes and by computing positive-length stops in `Chr` units while rejecting the old null-terminated wide-string API usage, but Stage 02 did not dynamically validate the fixed image.

source.description: First project statement that turns attacker-controlled input into the dispatch key for the vulnerable wide-decoder path.
source.value_from:
The saved witness `gt_results/arvo_16531/poc` is 388 bytes (sha256 `ab599fe34157547d4f71c41b1536aee081f04b7269c7c837db1498a8edcc9cab`). Its first 26 bytes are ASCII `dolang=e
encoding=utf-16

`; a hexdump shows `encoding=utf-16` at offsets 0x09..0x18. During `new_convert(*c, user_enc, sys_enc, NormFrom)`, that attacker-controlled setting reaches `fix_encoding_str()` and is normalized here to `ucs-2`, the key that selects the later `DecodeDirect<unsigned short>` path.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: ASan crash site in the second wide decode. Once the stop pointer from step 10 is unreachable, this dereference becomes the 2-byte read that crosses the end of the heap input buffer.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow ... READ of size 2` at `common/convert.cpp:555:22` in `acommon::DecodeDirect<unsigned short>::decode`, with `Convert::convert`, `aspell_speller_suggest`, and `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` directly below it.

root_cause.description: The positive-length wide decode uses the raw byte count to form a `unsigned short *` stop pointer instead of validating and converting `size` into 2-byte element units; once `DocumentChecker` has already emitted a code-unit count as `tok.len`, an odd `size` makes the loop boundary unreachable.
root_cause.note: The fix replaces this with `reinterpret_cast<const Chr *>(in0) + size/sizeof(Chr)` and, in the same hunk, stores `sizeof(Chr)` widths when appending wide characters. The witness needs both aspects: the first decode creates code-unit-length tokens, and the second decode trusts that odd length as a positive byte count.

tainted_value_origin.description: These fields are the concrete span values later passed as `size` and pointer offset to `aspell_speller_suggest()`. Because the preceding UTF-16 decode stored width 1, they represent UTF-16 code-unit counts rather than byte spans.

parser_admitted.description: After the fuzzer's blank-line-separated config prefix, `aspell_document_checker_process()` hands the remaining 362 bytes to Aspell's document parser through the configured wide converter. This is where the witness leaves configuration setup and enters the text-processing path that later yields the crashing suggestion token.

fine_trace.note:
Source. The 388-byte witness begins with the ASCII config prefix `dolang=e
encoding=utf-16

`. When `new_convert(*c, user_enc, sys_enc, NormFrom)` normalizes that attacker-controlled setting, this branch converts `utf-16` into `ucs-2`, the encoding key used to choose the later wide decoder.
The normalized key from step 1 selects `DecodeDirect<Uni16>`, so `speller->to_internal_` and the later suggestion conversion both interpret input as 2-byte code units.

After the 26-byte config prefix, the remaining 362 bytes of attacker-controlled document data are handed to `DocumentChecker` and decoded through the wide converter from step 2, populating `proc_str_` for tokenization.

During this first `DecodeDirect<unsigned short>::decode()` call, each `unsigned short` code unit is appended through the overload that defaults `FilterChar.width` to 1 (`FilterCharVector::append(FilterChar::Chr)` and `FilterChar(Chr, Width=1)`), even though each input element consumed 2 bytes. `proc_str_` therefore preserves code points but loses the original byte-width bookkeeping.

Tokenizer position bookkeeping reconstructs source spans by repeatedly adding `cur->width` while skipping non-word characters and while advancing through the word body. Because step 4 stored width 1 for every UTF-16 code unit, both `begin_pos` and `end_pos` become counts of code units rather than byte offsets into `data_str`.

These assignments copy the tokenizer positions into the exported `AspellToken`. The crashing iteration later reuses them as raw byte arguments at step 7; the saved overread in the second wide decode proves the resulting `tok.len` on that iteration was an odd positive count, i.e. not divisible by `sizeof(unsigned short)`.

The fuzzer loop invokes `aspell_speller_suggest()` with `data_str + tok.offset` and `tok.len` exactly as produced in step 6. No conversion back from UTF-16 code units to bytes occurs at this boundary.

The generated C API wrapper for `aspell_speller_suggest()` passes the same `in` and `size` into `to_internal_->convert`, and `Convert::convert()` immediately dispatches them to `decode_->decode`. The saved stack confirms this exact `aspell_speller_suggest -> Convert::convert` path.

Root cause. On the crashing suggestion call, `size` is the code-unit count from step 6, not a byte length aligned to 2. This line nevertheless forms `stop` from the raw byte address `in0 + size`, so the positive-size `for (; in != stop; ++in)` loop compares a 2-byte-stride pointer against an address that is one byte off that stride and cannot be reached.

Sink. Because `stop` is unreachable, each loop iteration keeps dereferencing `*in` and advancing by 2 bytes until the read at this line lands at the first address past the 388-byte heap buffer. AddressSanitizer reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 2` here, matching the saved stack `DecodeDirect<unsigned short>::decode -> Convert::convert -> aspell_speller_suggest -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`.

allocation_context.note: ASan reports the invalid read is 0 bytes to the right of the 388-byte heap region allocated by the AFL driver when it loads the saved witness.

format.contract:
Exactly the 388-byte witness stored in `gt_results/arvo_16531/poc` (sha256 `ab599fe34157547d4f71c41b1536aee081f04b7269c7c837db1498a8edcc9cab`). Its first 26 bytes are the ASCII config block `dolang=e
encoding=utf-16

`; the remaining 362 bytes are the document passed to `aspell_document_checker_process()`. For this exact witness, Aspell normalizes the config to `ucs-2`, uses `DecodeDirect<unsigned short>` for both document checking and suggestion conversion, emits a misspelling token whose `tok.len` is later reused as a raw byte length, and the second wide decode overruns by 2 bytes at `common/convert.cpp:555`. Stage 02 does not generalize beyond this saved witness.
